events.description:
Flaten Art Museum Exhibition – Michon Weeks: Mystic Topographies

For Michon Weeks, painting is a contemplative practice akin to meditation and prayer. Working in egg tempera, oil, and acrylic, Weeks paints the quiet terrain of everyday life: yards, tree lines, and utility poles. But these paintings do not describe the ordinary elements of the Minnesota landscape. They are the artist’s method for slow, sustained presence—and an invitation to the viewer to stay with something long enough for meaning to surface.

This body of work has emerged alongside a sustained creative exchange with author, scholar, and fellow St. Olaf professor Trish Zimmerman. Audio excerpts from the mystics, read and recorded by Weeks and Zimmerman, invite visitors to explore the sacred mystery of perception.
events.title: Michon Weeks: Mystic Topographies

events.description: Marking a quarter of a century since the September 11, 2001 attacks, the Flaten Art Museum highlights a print series from its collection: Thirty-Six Views of One World Trade Center by St. Olaf alumna Brenda Berkman ’73. Berkman — the sole named class plaintiff who opened the New York City Fire Department to women firefighters in 1982 — was a fire officer and first responder at the World Trade Center on 9/11, witnessing the destruction and loss that reverberated across the country.
events.title: Brenda Berkman ’73: Thirty-Six Views of One World Trade Center

The 16th Sunday after Pentecost; Sunday Worship with Holy Communion.

Associate College Chaplain Sarah Semmler Smith ’04 will deliver the sermon, presided by College Chaplain Matthew Marohl and assisted by Jonathan Madden ’20, Interim Cantor for the Student Congregation. The St. Olaf Choir will be conducted by Anton Armstrong ’78, Tosdal Professor of Music. The St. Olaf Choir, with 75 mixed voices, is the premier a cappella choir in the United States. For over a century, the choir has set a standard of choral excellence and remained at the forefront of choral artistry. Conducted since 1990 by Anton Armstrong, the St. Olaf Choir continues to develop the tradition that originated with its founder, F. Melius Christiansen.

events.description: What does it mean to realize you’re standing inside a historic moment — not just witnessing it, but shaping it? Firefighter and 9/11 first responder Brenda Berkman ’73 joins Visiting Assistant Professor of History Patrick Wilz to explore what it means to be swept into the current of history, and how one makes sense of it afterward. Drawing on Berkman’s service on September 11th and her printmaking practice in its aftermath, the conversation turns to how we process, commemorate, and remember trauma — both personally and collectively.
events.title: In Conversation: Brenda Berkman ’73 and Patrick Wilz on Memory, Service, and Meaning
